papers.title: Macrogenomic analysis showcases the diversity of tick RNA viruses in Mentougou, Beijing, China.
papers.abstract: Ticks are the second most significant vector of human pathogens worldwide, with 911 documented species globally and a broad distributed across China. Currently, over 160 tick-borne viruses (TBVs) have been identified, several of which pose substantial threats to human health, such as Dabie bandavirus, Jingmen tick virus, Alongshan virus, Songling virus, Beiji nairovirus, and Langya henipavirus, raising increasing global attention. Despite their significance, the diversity of TBVs in Beijing remains poorly characterized.
papers.summary: This study uses macrogenomic analysis to characterize the diversity of RNA viruses carried by ticks in Mentougou, Beijing, China, revealing a wide range of tick-borne viruses and highlighting the region's under-explored viral diversity. The findings underscore the need for enhanced surveillance of tick-borne pathogens in this area to mitigate potential public health risks.

papers.title: Longitudinal Exploratory Analysis of Salivary Microbiota Profiles in Patients with Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma Before and After Surgery: A Pilot Study.
papers.abstract: Salivary microbiome profiling may represent a promising non-invasive approach for characterizing OSCC-associated microbial patterns and longitudinal microbiome dynamics during patient management. This exploratory pilot study aimed to longitudinally assess salivary microbiota profiles in patients with oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) before and after tumor resection using Oxford Nanopore Technology. Unstimulated saliva samples were collected from 16 patients with OSCC at two time points (before and after tumor resection) and from 10 OSCC-free reference subjects. Microbial DNA was extracted u
papers.summary: This pilot study used Oxford Nanopore Technology to longitudinally profile salivary microbiota in 16 oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) patients before and after tumor resection, comparing them to 10 healthy controls. The findings suggest that salivary microbiome profiles shift after surgery, highlighting the potential of non-invasive salivary microbiome monitoring for OSCC management.

papers.title: Aspalathin-Rich Rooibos Tea Extract Regulates Hepatic Lipid Metabolism and Gut Microbiota in High-Fat Diet Fed Mice.
papers.abstract: Background: Hepatic lipid metabolism disorder has been linked to a wide range of diseases. Aspalathin is a flavonoid enriched in rooibos tea and has shown capacity to protect against hyperlipidemia, oxidative stress and inflammation. In the current study, we investigated the functional role of aspalathin in regulating liver metabolism and gut microbiota in the context of a high-fat diet (HFD). Methods: Male mice were fed a control diet or HFD, then HFD-fed animals were treated with or without aspalathin-rich extract (ASE). Hepatic neutral lipids were detected using oil red O staining and a col
papers.summary: This study demonstrates that an aspalathin-rich rooibos tea extract alleviates high-fat diet-induced hepatic lipid accumulation and modulates gut microbiota composition in mice, suggesting a potential dietary intervention for metabolic disorders. The findings support the role of aspalathin in regulating liver metabolism and gut microbial balance.

papers.title: Clinical Improvement and Taxonomic-Functional Gut Microbiome Remodeling After Six Months of Multi-Strain Synbiotic Supplementation in Mexican Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Gut dysbiosis in children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) has been associated with alterations in microbial ecology and metabolic function that may contribute to gastrointestinal dysfunction and the severity of clinical manifestations. Synbiotic and probiotic supplementation has emerged as a promising microbiome-targeted strategy for ASD; however, its effects on gut microbiome composition, functional potential, and clinical outcomes remain incompletely understood. We conducted a longitudinal study of Mexican children diagnosed with ASD to analyze changes in the compo
papers.summary: This longitudinal study in Mexican children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) found that six months of multi-strain synbiotic supplementation led to clinical improvement and significant remodeling of the gut microbiome's taxonomic and functional composition. The results support the potential of synbiotics as a microbiome-targeted intervention to alleviate ASD symptoms, though the study's scope is specific to this population and intervention.

papers.title: Effects of Non-Surgical Periodontal Therapy on Dental Plaque Microbiome.
papers.abstract: Periodontitis, a chronic inflammatory disease affecting approximately 40% of U.S. adults aged 30 years and older, is characterized by dysbiosis of the dental plaque microbiome. However, although scaling and root planing (SRP) is the cornerstone of periodontal treatment, its effects on the taxonomic composition and functional potential of the dental plaque microbiome remain incompletely understood. In this study, we used whole-metagenome shotgun sequencing to characterize taxonomic composition and functional potential in dental plaque microbiomes collected from 39 patients with Stage II or III
papers.summary: This study uses whole-metagenome shotgun sequencing to characterize how non-surgical periodontal therapy (scaling and root planing) affects the taxonomic composition and functional potential of the dental plaque microbiome in 39 patients with Stage II or III periodontitis. The findings provide a detailed view of microbiome changes associated with treatment, which may inform therapeutic monitoring and understanding of periodontal disease.

papers.title: Primer-Less Species Identification Throughout Fungal (Tuber magnatum), Plant (Corylus avellana) and Animal (Eisenia fetida) Kingdoms by Direct RNA Sequencing.
papers.abstract: Accurate species identification is essential for biodiversity studies, ecological monitoring, and biosecurity, but current molecular approaches rely on PCR amplification, which requires universal primers. Here, we evaluated the possibility of primer-free species identification via direct RNA sequencing (dRNA-seq) by using Oxford Nanopore Technology (ONT). Total RNA isolated from three major eukaryotic kingdoms-fungal (Tuber magnatum Picco 1788), plant (Corylus avellana L. 1753), and animal (Eisenia fetida Savigny 1826) specimens-was sequenced without reverse transcription and PCR amplification
papers.summary: This study demonstrates that direct RNA sequencing (dRNA-seq) using Oxford Nanopore Technology can identify species across three eukaryotic kingdoms (fungi, plant, animal) without the need for PCR amplification or universal primers. By sequencing total RNA directly from Tuber magnatum, Corylus avellana, and Eisenia fetida, the authors show that primer-free species identification is feasible, potentially simplifying biodiversity and biosecurity workflows.

papers.title: Preoperative prebiotic supplementation alleviates colitis and improves anastomotic healing associated with modulation of the gut microbiota in rats.
papers.abstract: Anastomotic leak is among the most feared complications in colorectal surgery. Patients with inflammatory bowel disease are particularly susceptible to impaired anastomotic healing, partially because of bacterial dysbiosis. Aiming to improve anastomotic healing, we examined the role of microbiota-targeted prehabilitation with a complex prebiotic supplement containing arabinogalactan, humic substances, and micronutrients in a rat model of experimental colitis.
papers.summary: This study tested a prebiotic supplement in a rat model of colitis and found that it reduced inflammation and improved surgical anastomotic healing, likely by modulating the gut microbiota. The results suggest that prebiotic prehabilitation could be a promising strategy to lower anastomotic leak risk in patients with inflammatory bowel disease.

papers.title: Metagenomic analysis of commensal small mammal samples from an international cargo shipping area, Bangkok Port, reveals potential zoonotic pathogens and implications for One Health surveillance.
papers.abstract: Commensal small mammals, such as rats and shrews, are recognized reservoirs for numerous zoonotic pathogens; however, their role in pathogen circulation at transport hubs remains underexplored. This study employs shotgun metagenomic sequencing to characterize microbial communities and assess zoonotic potential in tissue samples from commensal small mammals captured at Bangkok Port, an international cargo shipping hub in Thailand between June and August 2025. Following host read depletion, taxonomic profiling was performed to identify bacterial taxa of public health relevance, including sequenc
papers.summary: This study used shotgun metagenomic sequencing to characterize microbial communities in commensal small mammals (rats and shrews) captured at Bangkok Port, an international shipping hub, and identified potential zoonotic pathogens. The findings highlight the role of transport hubs in pathogen circulation and underscore the importance of One Health surveillance at such interfaces.

papers.title: Modeling microbiome modulation of tumor metabolic networks to predict synergistic therapies.
papers.abstract: Differences in microbiome composition profoundly influence drug response, yet methods to model the metabolic impact of microbes on host cells and therapeutics remain limited. We present a microbiome-aware computational framework combining machine learning and genome-scale metabolic models to predict combination therapies for colorectal cancer (CRC) in the presence of Fusobacterium nucleatum (Fn) and other pathogenic, probiotic, and commensal microbes. The model learned predictive metabolic flux signatures from 6,514 drug combination profiles in CRC cell lines and predicted synergistic drug com
papers.summary: This paper presents a computational framework that integrates machine learning with genome-scale metabolic models to predict how the microbiome influences drug responses in colorectal cancer. The model identifies synergistic drug combinations in the presence of Fusobacterium nucleatum and other microbes, offering a new approach to microbiome-aware therapy design.

papers.title: Blood and gut virome remodeling in gastric cancer: Anellovirus expansion and novel virus discovery.
papers.abstract: Gastric cancer (GC) is a prevalent malignancy worldwide, yet effective early diagnostic tools remain lacking, and the role of the virome, a key component of the tumor microenvironment, in GC progression is largely unknown. This study aimed to characterize the virome landscapes in peripheral blood and feces of GC patients versus healthy controls, and to identify viral signatures associated with GC onset and metastasis. We performed viral metagenomic sequencing on pooled libraries from 100 GC patients (45 non-metastatic, 55 metastatic) and 50 healthy controls, followed by taxonomic annotation, d
papers.summary: This study characterizes the blood and gut virome in gastric cancer patients, revealing an expansion of Anelloviruses and identifying novel viruses associated with disease and metastasis. These findings suggest that virome composition could serve as a potential biomarker for gastric cancer, though further validation is needed.

papers.title: Dental wastewater reveals a hidden reservoir of oral bacteriophage diversity.
papers.abstract: Bacteriophages (phages) are being explored as alternatives or complements to antibiotics because of their ability to selectively kill bacterial pathogens. However, phages that infect many oral bacteria remain undiscovered. Here, we discovered that dental wastewater harbors previously underexplored phage diversity. Viral particles concentrated from dental wastewater displayed diverse morphologies, including abundant filamentous phage-like particles. Deep long-read metagenomic sequencing of concentrated viral particles generated 7.4 billion bases of sequence data and yielded 255 medium- to high-
papers.summary: This study reveals that dental wastewater is a rich, previously untapped source of novel bacteriophages that infect oral bacteria. By using deep long-read metagenomic sequencing, the authors identified 255 medium- to high-quality phage genomes, greatly expanding the known diversity of oral phages and providing a valuable resource for phage therapy development.

papers.title: Virome DNA stable isotope probing reveals diverse active soil virus communities across ecosystem contexts.
papers.abstract: Viruses are increasingly recognized as important players in soil ecosystems, but the active lytic virus populations that influence microbe-mediated terrestrial ecosystem processes remain mostly uncharacterized. Here, we trace 13C-labeled glucose from host microorganisms into virus genomic DNA to identify virus populations actively involved in soil carbon (C) cycling, i.e., viruses that lysed 13C-incorporating microbes. We present experimental evidence of isotope labeling (i.e., lytic activity) of more than 5,000 virus populations. The active viruses lysed hosts from 197 microbial families acro
papers.summary: This study uses DNA stable isotope probing (SIP) to track 13C-labeled glucose from soil microbes into virus genomes, identifying over 5,000 virus populations that are actively lysing hosts and thus involved in soil carbon cycling. The active viruses target hosts from 197 microbial families, revealing diverse and ecosystem-specific lytic virus communities across different soil contexts.

papers.title: Exploring the hypothetical role of Bacteroides species in depression progression: insights from metagenomic analysis.
papers.abstract: Depression, a psychiatric disorder with significant morbidity and mortality, has a complex etiology. Recent advances in microbiome research have highlighted the potential role of fecal microbiota in depression pathogenesis. This study utilized shotgun metagenomic sequencing to compare the fecal microbiota of 28 depression patients and 26 healthy individuals. Significant differences in fecal microbiota composition were observed between the two groups. We generated 350 non-redundant high-quality metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) by binning and conducted comparisons between the depression and c
papers.summary: This study used shotgun metagenomic sequencing to compare the gut microbiomes of depression patients and healthy controls, finding significant compositional differences and generating 350 high-quality metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs). The results suggest a potential role for Bacteroides species in depression progression, offering new insights into the gut-brain axis.

papers.title: A qPCR-based approach targeting the microbial gene marker nanA of mucin-degrading Akkermansia in Parkinson's disease.
papers.abstract: BackgroundParkinson's disease (PD) is a multifactorial neurodegenerative disorder increasingly linked to gut microbiota alterations. However, despite advances in fecal microbiota profiling as a non-invasive approach to disease risk assessment, its clinical utility remains limited by a lack of functionally relevant microbial biomarkers.ObjectiveThis cross-sectional study aimed to identify a microbial gene marker reflecting metabolic potential associated with both the presence and severity of PD.MethodsFecal samples from patients with PD (n = 59) and healthy controls (n = 65) were analyzed by 16
papers.summary: This study developed a qPCR assay targeting the nanA gene of mucin-degrading Akkermansia and tested it on fecal samples from Parkinson's disease patients and healthy controls. The findings suggest that this functional microbial gene marker may be associated with PD presence and severity, offering a potential non-invasive biomarker.

papers.title: Natural transformation drives large-scale genome mosaicism in human gut bifidobacteria.
papers.abstract: Although horizontal gene transfer drives bacterial diversification, its contribution to chromosome-scale variation in human gut commensals remains unclear. This study demonstrated that human-associated bifidobacteria undergo extensive chromosomal transfer through natural transformation. Comparative genomics of coexisting Bifidobacterium pseudocatenulatum isolates from a single individual revealed extensive recombination signatures between the lineages. We experimentally reproduced this recombination by co-culturing strains, resulting in the transfer of multiple chromosomal regions and generati
papers.summary: This study shows that human gut bifidobacteria can exchange large chromosomal regions through natural transformation, creating extensive genome mosaicism. Comparative genomics of coexisting strains from one individual revealed recombination signatures, which were experimentally reproduced in co-culture, demonstrating that this process drives chromosome-scale variation in gut commensals.

papers.title: A three-metabolite microbiota-associated signature for early risk stratification of gestational diabetes mellitus.
papers.abstract: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes and long-term metabolic and cardiovascular risk. However, oral glucose tolerance testing at 24-28 gestational weeks limits early risk stratification. Gut microbiota-associated metabolites may reflect early metabolic abnormalities, including those relevant to cardiometabolic health, but robust early-pregnancy biomarkers remain limited.
papers.summary: This study identifies a three-metabolite signature derived from gut microbiota-associated metabolites that can stratify the risk of gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) early in pregnancy, potentially before the standard 24-28 week oral glucose tolerance test. The findings suggest that these metabolites could serve as early biomarkers for GDM, enabling earlier intervention and improved maternal and fetal outcomes.

papers.title: Longitudinal profiling of upper respiratory tract microbiota and metabolome in hospitalized COVID-19 convalescents: a 3-year prospective cohort study.
papers.abstract: Long COVID is characterized by persistent, far-reaching effects in convalescent individuals, with pulmonary diffusion impairment emerging as a clinically impactful sequela affecting more than one-third of this population. The salivary microbiome and metabolome, reflecting the oral-lung axis, offer a window into the mechanisms underlying this condition. However, systematic longitudinal evidence on their long-term dynamics after infection and their predictive value for persistent pulmonary diffusion impairment remains scarce.
papers.summary: This 3-year prospective study tracked the upper respiratory tract microbiome and metabolome in COVID-19 convalescents, revealing persistent alterations and identifying specific microbial and metabolic signatures associated with long-term pulmonary diffusion impairment. The findings suggest that oral-lung axis profiles could serve as predictive biomarkers for this clinically significant long COVID sequela.

papers.title: The gut-immune-brain axis in CNS tumors: Causal roles of microbiota and inflammatory proteins unveiled by Mendelian randomization and single-cell transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: There is a growing number of research suggesting that there is an association between gut microbiota and central nervous system (CNS) tumor. However, the causal relationships and the mediation effects of inflammatory proteins in the associations are unclear. We extracted genetic variants associated with gut microbiota, inflammatory proteins, and 4 subtypes of CNS tumors from published genome-wide association studies and performed a Mendelian randomization analysis to identify potential causal effects. The inverse variance weighted method was used as the main method. Mediation analysis and sing
papers.summary: This study uses Mendelian randomization and single-cell transcriptomics to investigate causal relationships between gut microbiota, inflammatory proteins, and CNS tumors, identifying potential mediating roles of inflammatory proteins. The findings suggest specific microbial taxa and inflammatory pathways may influence CNS tumor risk, offering new insights into the gut-immune-brain axis.

papers.title: Causal associations between gut microbiota and five common oral lesions: A two-sample Mendelian randomization study.
papers.abstract: Previous studies have investigated the relationship between gut microbiota (GM) and oral lesions, but the reported associations across microbial taxa and oral conditions have been inconsistent. This 2-sample Mendelian randomization study using summary-level GWAS data aimed to clarify the causal links between GM and 5 oral conditions: loose teeth, toothache, bleeding gums, painful gums, and mouth ulcers. GM data were obtained from the MiBioGen consortium, while outcome data were derived from the Neale Lab and MRC-IEU consortium. We applied inverse variance weighted (IVW) and complementary MR me
papers.summary: This study used Mendelian randomization with GWAS summary data to investigate causal links between gut microbiota and five common oral conditions (loose teeth, toothache, bleeding gums, painful gums, mouth ulcers). The findings suggest potential causal associations for specific microbial taxa, though the effects vary by condition.

papers.title: Sustainable Protein Transitions: A Comprehensive Review of Insect Meal in Broiler Diets-Nutritional Value, Immunomodulatory Effects, Gut Health Interactions, and Future Perspectives.
papers.abstract: Broiler production keeps intensifying, and the environmental cost of the protein sources that feed it, principally soybean meal and fishmeal, has become harder to justify. Insect meal, derived chiefly from black soldier fly larvae (Hermetia illucens), yellow mealworm (Tenebrio molitor), and housefly larvae (Musca domestica), has emerged as a candidate able to address nutritional, immunological, and ecological goals at once. This review evaluates the evidence on the nutritional composition, digestibility, growth performance, immunomodulatory mechanisms, and gut health effects of insect meal in
papers.summary: This review evaluates insect meal (from black soldier fly larvae, yellow mealworm, and housefly larvae) as a sustainable protein alternative in broiler diets, covering its nutritional value, digestibility, growth performance, immunomodulatory effects, and gut health impacts. It concludes that insect meal can support broiler production while reducing environmental costs, though further research is needed on optimal inclusion levels and long-term effects.

papers.title: Convergent Gut Microbiome Remodeling Across Ischemic Stroke, Myocardial Infarction, and Longevity Reveals a Shared Ecological Signature of Aging and Disease.
papers.abstract: Gut microbiota dysbiosis has been associated with ischemic stroke (IS), myocardial infarction (MI), and aging, but whether these contexts share reproducible microbial features remains unclear. We conducted an exploratory and hypothesis-generating descriptive study of genus-level microbiota patterns across an internal IS cohort and publicly available external IS, MI, and age-stratified or longevity-associated datasets. Analyses were performed within predefined age strata and interpreted cautiously because of the small internal cohort, cross-cohort heterogeneity, and the absence of direct metabo
papers.summary: This study investigates whether gut microbiome changes are shared across ischemic stroke, myocardial infarction, and aging. By analyzing internal and public datasets, the authors identify a convergent ecological signature of dysbiosis common to these conditions, suggesting a shared microbial pattern associated with aging and disease. The findings are exploratory and require cautious interpretation due to cohort heterogeneity and limited sample sizes.

papers.title: Zoo gut plastispheres enable pathogen escape and adaptation.
papers.abstract: In zoos, intensive human contact and artificial feeding may create pathways for microplastic (MP) ingestion and gut colonization. We hypothesized that ingested MPs form intestinal plastispheres with elevated pathogenic potential and enhanced environmental persistence. To test this, we surveyed feces from 15 zoo-dwelling species and coupled particle characterization, feces-derived intestinal simulations, metagenomic sequencing, and a subsequent water-exposure experiment. Zoo feces contained more abundant MPs than reported for wild counterparts, with fragments predominating and polyethylene tere
papers.summary: This study investigates microplastic (MP) ingestion in zoo animals, finding that zoo feces contain higher MP levels than wild counterparts and that ingested MPs form 'plastispheres' in the gut with elevated pathogenic potential and environmental persistence. Using metagenomics and simulations, the authors show that these plastispheres enable pathogen escape and adaptation, highlighting a potential health risk in human-animal interfaces.

papers.title: Response of marine benthic viral communities to anthropogenic disturbances.
papers.abstract: Viruses are key regulators of microbial mortality, gene flow, and metabolic functioning in marine sediments, yet their responses to different forms of anthropogenic disturbance remain poorly understood. Here, we present the first comparative viral metagenomic analysis of benthic viral communities across two major but contrasting disturbance regimes: organic enrichment beneath salmon aquaculture farms and crude-oil contamination near offshore oil installations. Using 123 sediment metagenomes from Scotland and Norway, we assessed how virus diversity, taxonomic composition, and community structur
papers.journal: The Science of the total environment
papers.summary: This study presents the first comparative viral metagenomic analysis of benthic viral communities under two contrasting anthropogenic disturbances—organic enrichment from salmon aquaculture and crude-oil contamination—using 123 sediment metagenomes from Scotland and Norway. The findings reveal how virus diversity, taxonomic composition, and community structure respond to these disturbances, providing new insights into the ecological impacts of human activities on marine benthic viral communities.

papers.title: Human wastewater contamination drives the emergence of multidrug-resistant bacteria in the Galápagos marine ecosystem.
papers.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance poses a global threat to public health. Mobile microbiological laboratories can enable environmental monitoring of antimicrobial resistance, particularly in geographically remote and resource-limited locations, such as the Galápagos archipelago. Here, we report the development of a mobile laboratory for antimicrobial resistance surveillance of marine sites surrounding San Cristóbal, the archipelago's second most populated island, which has experienced rapid urbanization and intense international tourism pressure. On-site metagenomic sequencing of wastewater-contaminate
papers.summary: This study used a mobile laboratory to perform on-site metagenomic sequencing of marine samples around San Cristóbal Island in the Galápagos, revealing that human wastewater contamination is driving the emergence of multidrug-resistant bacteria in the marine ecosystem. The findings highlight the utility of portable sequencing for antimicrobial resistance surveillance in remote, resource-limited settings and underscore the environmental impact of urbanization and tourism.

papers.title: Alcohol Consumption and Gut Microbiota-Derived Metabolites in Primates: A Systematic Review.
papers.abstract: Alcohol consumption has been increasingly associated with alterations in the gut microbiota and its metabolic activity; however, evidence regarding microbiota-derived metabolites remains fragmented. This systematic review aimed to synthesize current evidence on the effects of alcohol consumption on gut microbiota-derived metabolites in humans and non-human primates. The review was conducted according to Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines and included studies published between 2012 and 2026. Searches were performed in PubMed, Web of Science, S
papers.summary: This systematic review synthesizes evidence from primate and human studies on how alcohol consumption alters gut microbiota-derived metabolites, highlighting fragmented but suggestive links between alcohol intake and changes in microbial metabolic activity. It underscores the need for more standardized research to clarify these effects.

papers.title: Transformation of Agro-Industrial By-Products into High-Value Animal-Derived Foods: Bioactive Compounds, Microbiome-Mediated Biotransformation, Metabolomic Traceability and Circular Valorization.
papers.abstract: Agro-industrial by-products are increasingly considered as feed resources for circular animal production, but their value should not be interpreted only as a low-cost replacement of conventional ingredients. This scoping review critically examines how by-products from grape, olive, tomato, citrus, cereal, brewery, oilseed and vegetable processing chains may contribute to the development of high-value animal-derived foods. Particular attention is given to bioactive compounds, polyphenols, carotenoids, tocopherols, fermentable fibres and residual lipids, as well as to microbiome-mediated biotran
papers.summary: This scoping review examines how agro-industrial by-products (from grape, olive, tomato, citrus, cereal, brewery, oilseed, and vegetable processing) can be used not just as low-cost feed replacements but to create high-value animal-derived foods. It focuses on bioactive compounds, polyphenols, carotenoids, tocopherols, fermentable fibers, and residual lipids, and highlights the role of the microbiome in biotransformation and the potential for metabolomic traceability in circular valorization.

papers.title: Marked dominance of Actinomycetota and compositional shifts in bacterial communities in Brazilian dryland soils under land-use change.
papers.abstract: Tropical dry forests are among the most threatened and least studied tropical forest ecosystems worldwide. The Caatinga, the largest tropical dry forest in South America, comprises preserved and agriculturally impacted areas, providing a valuable model system to investigate how semiarid soil bacterial communities respond to natural seasonality and land-use change. Here, we evaluated how land-use and seasonality shape microbial community structure and ecological strategies in soils from conserved forest (CEF) and agriculture-influenced areas (BEF) across rainy and dry seasons using a contig-bas
papers.summary: This study characterizes soil bacterial communities in Brazil's Caatinga dry forest, revealing that Actinomycetota dominates and that land-use change from conserved forest to agriculture significantly alters community composition and ecological strategies across seasons. The findings highlight the sensitivity of semiarid soil microbiomes to anthropogenic disturbance.

papers.title: Biological contributions to manganese oxides in rock varnish at Murujuga (Western Australia).
papers.abstract: Rock varnish is a ubiquitous Mn-rich coating on exposed rock surfaces in arid environments, yet the mechanisms underlying its formation remain debated. Here, we investigate rock varnish from Murujuga, Western Australia, to assess the role of microbial processes in manganese (Mn) accumulation. Bulk compositional and mineralogical analyses confirm high concentrations of Mn, Fe, Al, and Si; however, the Mn matrix is predominantly composed of amorphous to poorly crystalline phases that fall below the indexing or detection thresholds of X-ray diffraction (XRD) and electron backscatter diffraction (
papers.summary: This study examines rock varnish from Murujuga, Western Australia, to determine whether microbial processes contribute to manganese oxide formation. The authors find that the Mn-rich matrix is largely amorphous and poorly crystalline, and they assess biological contributions to its formation, providing new insights into the debated mechanisms of rock varnish development in arid environments.

papers.title: Potential plastic biodegradation in lakes worldwide.
papers.abstract: Plastic pollution is ubiquitous, yet the biodegradation of plastic waste remains poorly understood due to limited knowledge of microbial plastic degradation potential. Here, we demonstrate that plastic waste shapes the global distribution of plastic-degrading potential across 182,661 lakes worldwide using integrated metagenomic and machine learning analyses and identify a tipping point (≥7.44 particles/m3) for effective in situ bioremediation. We constructed, for the first time, a catalog of candidate plastic-degrading bacteria, including 15,715 nonredundant enzyme homologs and 4,856 metagenom
papers.summary: This study maps the global distribution of microbial plastic-degrading potential across 182,661 lakes using metagenomics and machine learning, revealing that plastic waste shapes this potential and identifying a tipping point (≥7.44 particles/m³) for effective in situ bioremediation. The authors constructed a comprehensive catalog of candidate plastic-degrading bacteria, including 15,715 nonredundant enzyme homologs and 4,856 metagenomic species, providing a foundational resource for understanding and harnessing microbial plastic degradation.

papers.title: B-MASTER: scalable Bayesian multivariate regression for master predictor discovery in colorectal cancer microbiome-metabolite profiles.
papers.abstract: The gut microbiome shapes cancer therapy response through its influence on host metabolism. While prior studies examine pairwise associations between individual genera and metabolites, there is limited methodology for identifying microbial genera that systematically regulate the overall metabolome. Scalable statistical tools are needed to uncover such system-level "master predictors" in high-dimensional microbiome-metabolome data.
papers.summary: This paper introduces B-MASTER, a scalable Bayesian multivariate regression method for identifying microbial genera that act as 'master predictors' of the overall metabolome in colorectal cancer. It addresses the limitation of pairwise association studies by enabling system-level analysis of high-dimensional microbiome-metabolome data, potentially improving understanding of how the gut microbiome influences cancer therapy response.

papers.title: Quantifying the aromatic amino acid metabolome: UPLC-MS/MS analysis of aromatic amino acids and their host and co-metabolites in plasma.
papers.abstract: Aromatic amino acids (AAAs), tryptophan, phenylalanine, and tyrosine along with their pathway metabolites have been implicated in the pathogenesis of diseases ranging from cardiovascular, neurological, inflammatory, and cancer diseases, among others. As such, the measurement of the primary AAAs, their host pathway metabolites, and microbiome derived co-metabolites in blood can provide a sensitive reflection of systemic health. The aim of the study was to develop a method for the quantification of 17 metabolites, the three AAAs and various of their metabolites in plasma using a high-throughput
papers.journal: Journal of chromatography. B, Analytical technologies in the biomedical and life sciences
papers.summary: This paper presents a new UPLC-MS/MS method for quantifying 17 aromatic amino acid metabolites in plasma, including host-derived pathway metabolites and microbiome co-metabolites. The method enables high-throughput measurement of these compounds, which are relevant to cardiovascular, neurological, inflammatory, and cancer diseases, providing a tool for assessing systemic health.

papers.title: Genome-Resolved Metagenomics Reveals Thermophilic Microbial Diversity and Putative Hydrolase-Encoding Genes in the El Tatio Geothermal Field.
papers.abstract: Geothermal ecosystems constitute important reservoirs of thermophilic microorganisms and their associated metabolic functions; however, the genome-resolved diversity and enzymatic potential of high-altitude geothermal systems remain poorly characterized. Here, we applied shotgun metagenomics and genome-resolved approaches to investigate thermophilic microbial communities inhabiting geothermal sediments from the El Tatio geothermal field, a polyextreme hydrothermal system located at ~4300 m above sea level in the Andean Altiplano of northern Chile. Genome reconstruction yielded 657 metagenome-a
papers.summary: This study used shotgun metagenomics and genome-resolved approaches to characterize the thermophilic microbial communities in sediments from the El Tatio geothermal field in the Chilean Andes, reconstructing 657 metagenome-assembled genomes. The analysis revealed high microbial diversity and identified numerous putative hydrolase-encoding genes, highlighting the enzymatic potential of this high-altitude geothermal ecosystem for biotechnological applications.

papers.title: De novo assembly and authentication of ancient DNA metagenomes with nf-core/mag.
papers.abstract: Ancient DNA provides a direct window into the evolutionary processes that have shaped living microbial species today, as well as their now extinct relatives. Advances in both sequencing methods and de novo assembly techniques have not only resulted in a flood of modern metagenomic sequencing data, but they have also allowed palaeogenomicists to retrieve vast amounts of ancient DNA from past microorganisms, including species and strains without modern reference genomes. However, the degraded nature of ancient DNA means that the standard techniques of genome assembly developed for modern DNA are
papers.summary: This paper presents nf-core/mag, a new bioinformatics pipeline for de novo assembly and authentication of ancient DNA metagenomes. It addresses the unique challenges of degraded ancient DNA, enabling researchers to reconstruct and validate genomes of past microorganisms without modern references.

papers.title: Integrated transcriptomic and hormonomic insights into cadmium tolerance of a Euglena mutabilis fungal-algal-bacterial consortium.
papers.abstract: Acidic, metal-contaminated environments harbour specialized microbial consortia adapted to extreme stress. We examined an environmental Euglena mutabilis culture naturally associated with Talaromyces and Acidiphilium acidophilum and exposed it to cadmium (Cd). Integrated transcriptomic, hormonal, structural and taxonomic analyses revealed a coordinated Cd-tolerance strategy. RNA sequencing showed differential regulation of metal transporters consistent with a shift from Cd uptake to intracellular sequestration. Transmission electron microscopy confirmed Cd compartmentalization within chloropla
papers.summary: This study reveals how a microbial consortium centered on the alga Euglena mutabilis tolerates cadmium stress through a coordinated strategy involving metal transporter regulation, intracellular sequestration, and hormonal signaling. Integrated transcriptomic and hormonomic analyses provide a systems-level view of the consortium's adaptive response, highlighting the potential of such natural communities for bioremediation.

papers.title: Predicting the plastic biodegradation potential within microbial lineages and across global ecosystems.
papers.abstract: Plastic waste pollution is a global issue that threatens biodiversity and human health. Current plastic waste management practices are not sufficient to keep up with increasing plastic production rates. Microorganisms have the capacity to degrade different types of bio-based and synthetic plastics through enzymatic reactions, offering an alternative solution to traditional plastic recycling techniques. A limited number of plastic-degrading enzymes have been identified, sequenced and characterized; however, studies exploring the distribution of homologues of these enzymes across habitats and mi
papers.summary: This study predicts the potential for plastic biodegradation across microbial lineages and global ecosystems by identifying homologues of known plastic-degrading enzymes. It reveals that such enzymes are more widespread than previously thought, with distinct distributions across habitats, suggesting a broader microbial capacity for plastic degradation that could inform bioremediation strategies.

papers.title: Nanopore Long-Read Metagenomics Reveals Pollution-Driven Antibiotic Resistance and Xenobiotic Degradation in Urban Beach Microbiomes.
papers.abstract: Coastal ecosystems are vital for biodiversity but are increasingly threatened by urbanisation and pollution, which significantly alter local microbial communities. This study assessed bacterial diversity and functional profiles in urban and island beaches in Belém, Brazil. Urban beaches showed significantly higher microbial diversity and evenness, alongside functional plasticity due to pollutant input, while island beaches hosted more specialised and stable communities. Taxonomic analysis revealed the significant enrichment of opportunistic genera such as Comamonas, Clostridium and Paenibacill
papers.summary: This study used nanopore long-read metagenomics to compare microbial communities in urban versus island beaches in Belém, Brazil, finding that urban beaches had higher microbial diversity and functional plasticity driven by pollution, with enrichment of opportunistic genera like Comamonas, Clostridium, and Paenibacillus. The results link pollution to increased antibiotic resistance and xenobiotic degradation potential in coastal microbiomes.

papers.title: Generation and Application of Ultra-Fine, Long-Term Stable Nanobubble Water: An Evaluation of Inclusion Effects on Aromatic Components and Antimicrobial Activity.
papers.abstract: Nano- and pico-bubble water (NPB), containing hydrogen or ozone, is widely used as a cleaning agent due to its bactericidal and antiviral properties. However, some products-such as certain hydrogen waters-contain only large bubbles or have an extremely low bubble count, making them sometimes indistinguishable from ordinary drinking water. To accurately evaluate NPB activity, we developed a method for producing ultra-nano-pico-bubble water (NanoGAS water [NGW]), an ultra-fine bubble water that is stable and non-volatile over extended periods. By combining a mixed gas-liquid fluid rotary mixer a
papers.summary: This study presents a method for generating ultra-fine, long-term stable nanobubble water (NanoGAS water) and evaluates its effects on aromatic components and antimicrobial activity. The authors demonstrate that their production method yields stable nanobubbles with high bubble counts, and they assess the inclusion of gases like hydrogen or ozone for potential cleaning and antimicrobial applications.

papers.title: Microbiota-Neuroinflammation Crosstalk in Primary Brain Tumors: Focus on Glioblastoma.
papers.abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) is the most aggressive primary brain tumor in adults and remains difficult to treat because of diffuse invasion, immunosuppression, metabolic adaptability, and therapy resistance. This review evaluates how gut microbiota and microbiota-associated neuroinflammatory signaling may contribute to GBM biology and therapeutic response.
papers.summary: This review examines the emerging role of gut microbiota and microbiota-associated neuroinflammatory signaling in glioblastoma (GBM) biology and treatment response. It highlights how the gut-brain axis may influence tumor progression, immunosuppression, and therapy resistance, suggesting a potential avenue for adjunctive therapeutic strategies.

papers.title: Domestication shapes the gut microbial structure and metabolic function in felids: a metagenomic study of wild and domestic cats.
papers.abstract: The domestication process has profoundly altered the dietary patterns and living conditions of cats, with corresponding effects on their gut microbiome.
papers.summary: This study uses metagenomics to compare the gut microbiomes of wild and domestic cats, revealing that domestication significantly alters both the microbial community structure and its metabolic functions, likely due to changes in diet and environment. The findings highlight how human-driven lifestyle changes shape the feline gut microbiome.

papers.title: Glacial meltwater is associated with gene-specific diversification of metal resistance genes in high Arctic soil microbiomes.
papers.abstract: Climate warming accelerates glacial meltwater delivery to Arctic lakes, mobilizing metals from thawing catchments and reshaping the selective landscape experienced by resident microbes. Whether these gradients leave detectable signatures of diversification in environmental resistance genes remains unclear. We investigated four metal resistance genes (merA, arsC, cadA, and chrR) in metagenomic datasets from Lake Hazen (Nunavut, Canada), the largest High Arctic freshwater lake, sampled across a natural hydrological gradient of Control, Low-runoff, and High-runoff regimes. Using a space-for-time
papers.summary: This study examines how glacial meltwater runoff in the High Arctic influences the diversification of metal resistance genes in soil microbiomes. By analyzing metagenomic data from Lake Hazen across a hydrological gradient, the authors found gene-specific diversification patterns linked to meltwater-associated metal exposure, suggesting that climate-driven runoff shapes microbial adaptation.

papers.title: Integrative multi-omics analysis identifies microbial dysbiosis and functional metabolic reprogramming in acute kidney injury.
papers.abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a life-threatening syndrome with high morbidity and mortality, yet its early diagnosis and underlying mechanisms remain poorly defined. Emerging evidence implicates gut dysbiosis and microbial metabolic dysfunction in AKI pathogenesis via the gut-kidney axis, yet a comprehensive, multi-omics characterization of microbial functional alterations in general AKI populations remains lacking.
papers.summary: This study uses an integrative multi-omics approach to characterize gut microbial dysbiosis and functional metabolic reprogramming in patients with acute kidney injury (AKI), revealing specific microbial and metabolic alterations linked to the gut-kidney axis. The findings provide a comprehensive resource that may aid in early diagnosis and understanding of AKI pathogenesis.

papers.title: Fish gut-water interface as a hotspot for the dissemination of antibiotic resistance genes across natural and aquaculture systems.
papers.abstract: Freshwater ecosystems are important reservoirs and transmission pathways for antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs), yet host-mediated microbial selection and anthropogenic pressure on fish gut resistome remain poorly characterised, especially in major South Asian river systems. We performed shotgun metagenomics and genome-resolved binning from 194 fish representing four species, along with host-associated water samples, collected from six geographically distinct sites spanning two major river systems (the Yamuna and the Indus) and two aquaculture farms. The fish gut nurtures distinct microbial co
papers.summary: This study uses shotgun metagenomics and genome-resolved binning on 194 fish and water samples from South Asian rivers and aquaculture farms to show that the fish gut-water interface is a hotspot for antibiotic resistance gene (ARG) dissemination. The fish gut harbors distinct microbial communities that facilitate the spread of ARGs, with anthropogenic pressure from aquaculture intensifying this effect.

papers.title: Functional genetic signatures of the gut microbiome in cardiometabolic diseases: mechanisms and translational opportunities.
papers.abstract: The human gut microbiome plays a very important role in the regulation of host metabolism and overall physiological homeostasis. Disruptions in microbial community function have been increasingly implicated in cardiometabolic diseases, including obesity, type 2 diabetes, cardiovascular disease, and metabolic dysfunction-associated liver disease. Advances in metagenomic sequencing have identified functional genetic signatures within the gut microbiome for short-chain fatty acid biosynthesis, bile acid metabolism, lipopolysaccharide (LPS) production, amino acid metabolism, trimethylamine N-oxide
papers.summary: This review synthesizes current knowledge on how functional genetic signatures of the gut microbiome—such as those involved in short-chain fatty acid biosynthesis, bile acid metabolism, and LPS production—contribute to cardiometabolic diseases. It highlights mechanistic links and discusses translational opportunities for microbiome-based diagnostics and therapeutics.

papers.title: Rhizosphere microbiomes in drought-tolerant and drought-sensitive bermudagrass genotypes: root exudate association.
papers.abstract: Plant-microbiome interactions in the rhizosphere are critical for plant adaptation to environmental stress; however, the coordinated roles of root exudates and microbiome dynamics remain poorly understood.
papers.summary: This study compares the rhizosphere microbiomes of drought-tolerant and drought-sensitive bermudagrass genotypes, revealing that drought tolerance is associated with distinct microbial communities and root exudate profiles. The findings suggest that specific root exudates may recruit beneficial microbes that help the plant cope with drought stress, providing insights into plant-microbiome interactions under environmental stress.

papers.title: Omics data in relative values are almost subcompositionally coherent.
papers.abstract: Omics data are compositional and often expressed as relative abundances after total sum scaling normalization. An important statistical issue with compositional data is the lack of subcompositional coherence, meaning that relative abundances change when data are re-normalized after removing or adding features. While this problem is well documented for small compositions, it has not been investigated in large Omics datasets, which typically contain hundreds or thousands of features and where subcompositions are ubiquitous. Subcompositions arise, for example, when using different reference datas
papers.summary: This paper investigates whether the lack of subcompositional coherence—a known issue in compositional data analysis—is practically relevant for large omics datasets with hundreds or thousands of features. The authors show that relative abundances (after total sum scaling) are almost subcompositionally coherent in such large datasets, meaning that re-normalization after removing or adding features has minimal impact. This finding suggests that concerns about subcompositional incoherence may be less critical for typical omics studies than previously thought.

papers.title: Calibrating tetranucleotide-frequency distances for metagenomic binning with right-skewed distribution models.
papers.abstract: Metagenomic binning is a pivotal step in reconstructing metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) from complex microbial communities, and it critically depends on reliable measures of similarity between contigs. In many workflows, tetranucleotide-frequency (TNF) distances are translated into probabilistic evidence of a shared genome of origin. Despite their central role, these distances are often modeled with convenient but poorly matched assumptions, even though they are intrinsically non-negative and frequently exhibit pronounced right-skewness-features that can distort tail behavior and weaken do
papers.summary: This paper introduces a calibration method for tetranucleotide-frequency (TNF) distances used in metagenomic binning, addressing the issue that these distances are non-negative and right-skewed, which conventional models handle poorly. By fitting right-skewed distribution models, the authors improve the accuracy of probabilistic evidence for contigs sharing a genome, potentially enhancing metagenomic binning performance.

papers.title: Effects of diarrhea and antibiotic-induced microbial elimination on dynamic changes in fecal microbial communities and antibiotic resistance of Hu sheep lambs (Ovis aries).
papers.abstract: As a highly reproductive meat sheep breed in China, Hu sheep is an important economic group in ruminant animal breeding. However, research on its intestinal microbiomes under the background of diarrhea and antibiotic treatment remains relatively limited.
papers.summary: This study examines how diarrhea and antibiotic treatment alter fecal microbial communities and antibiotic resistance in Hu sheep lambs, a key meat sheep breed in China. The findings reveal dynamic shifts in the microbiome and resistome, providing insights into the impact of antibiotic use on gut health in this economically important livestock.

papers.title: The composition alteration of gut microbiota in lung cancer: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: The association between the gut microbiota and lung cancer remains understudied. In this study, we conducted a comprehensive systematic review and meta-analysis to quantitatively synthesize evidence from multiple cohorts to identify robust and consistent alterations in gut microbial diversity and taxonomy associated with lung cancer.
papers.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis synthesizes evidence from multiple cohorts to identify consistent alterations in gut microbial diversity and taxonomy associated with lung cancer, providing a quantitative overview of the gut-lung axis. The findings highlight specific microbial changes that may serve as biomarkers or therapeutic targets, though the underlying mechanisms remain to be fully explored.

papers.title: Integrative bioinformatics analysis identifies gut microbiota-derived metabolite-associated immune candidate targets in high-risk primary biliary cholangitis.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to identify and prioritize gut microbiota-derived metabolite-associated host candidate targets in high-risk primary biliary cholangitis (PBC) through integrative multi-omics analysis and external validation.
papers.summary: This study uses integrative multi-omics analysis to identify gut microbiota-derived metabolite-associated host immune targets in high-risk primary biliary cholangitis (PBC), prioritizing candidate genes for further validation. The findings suggest specific metabolite-driven immune pathways that may contribute to PBC pathogenesis, offering potential biomarkers or therapeutic targets.

papers.title: Atopic dermatitis: pathogenesis, immunology, microbiome, and salivary biomarkers.
papers.abstract: Atopic dermatitis is a chronic inflammatory skin disease influenced by genetic predisposition, immune dysregulation, and environmental factors, as well as skin and gut microbiota. This review summarises the key mechanisms involved in this disease development, including disturbances in innate and adaptive immune responses, ethnic differences in immune pathways, and the contribution of microbial imbalance to skin barrier dysfunction. Special attention is given to salivary biomarkers-such as cortisol, melatonin, alpha-amylase, chromogranin A, C-reactive protein, and immunoglobulin A-which offer a
papers.summary: This review summarizes the pathogenesis of atopic dermatitis, focusing on immune dysregulation, ethnic differences, and the role of skin and gut microbiota in barrier dysfunction. It highlights the potential of salivary biomarkers (e.g., cortisol, melatonin, IgA) as non-invasive tools for diagnosis and monitoring.

papers.title: Placental and maternal microbiome adaptations in a preeclamptic-like mouse model.
papers.abstract: The maternal microbiome plays a crucial role in pregnancy with growing evidence supporting vertical microbial transmission from mother to fetus. The placenta, once considered sterile, may serve as a conduit for this transfer. We hypothesized that the placental microbial signatures would be distinctly different from oral, fecal, or vaginal microbiomes in pregnant mice.
papers.summary: This study characterizes the placental microbiome in a preeclamptic-like mouse model and compares it to maternal oral, fecal, and vaginal microbiomes, finding distinct microbial signatures in the placenta. The results suggest that placental microbial composition is uniquely adapted and may be influenced by pregnancy complications like preeclampsia, supporting the idea of vertical microbial transfer.

papers.title: Baseline characteristics of the HOMINY (human papillomavirus, human immunodeficiency virus, and oral microbiota interplay in Nigerian youth) prospective longitudinal cohort.
papers.abstract: The HOMINY (Human Papillomavirus, Human Immunodeficiency Virus, and Oral Microbiota Interplay in Nigerian Youth) cohort is a prospective longitudinal study established to investigate oral HPV infection and the oral microbiome among mother-child pairs with and without HIV in Nigeria. The objective of this analysis was to describe baseline demographic and clinical characteristics of the cohort, including HPV awareness, HPV vaccination, and cervical cancer screening practice by HIV status.
papers.summary: This paper describes the baseline characteristics of the HOMINY cohort, a prospective longitudinal study in Nigeria examining oral HPV infection and the oral microbiome in mother-child pairs with and without HIV. It reports demographic and clinical data, including HPV awareness, vaccination, and cervical cancer screening practices, stratified by HIV status. This foundational description provides essential context for future analyses of HPV and microbiome dynamics in this population.

papers.title: Paper mulberry in animal nutrition: processing, host responses, and product quality.
papers.abstract: Paper mulberry (Broussonetia papyrifera) has attracted increasing attention as a local feed resource because it combines perennial woody biomass, protein-rich foliage and diverse plant secondary compounds. Its feeding value depends on plant part, harvest stage, processing method, fermentation quality, target animal species and dietary inclusion level. This review examines paper mulberry from feed composition and processing to animal responses, product traits and proposed mechanisms. Current evidence is strongest in ruminants, where paper mulberry silage or fermented feed has been associated wi
papers.summary: This review examines the use of paper mulberry (Broussonetia papyrifera) as a feed resource for livestock, covering its nutritional composition, processing methods, and effects on animal performance and product quality. The evidence is strongest in ruminants, where fermented or ensiled paper mulberry shows potential benefits, though outcomes depend on factors like plant part, harvest stage, and inclusion level.

papers.title: Gut microbiota and serum metabolome in children with human metapneumovirus infection.
papers.abstract: To analyze the alterations in gut microbiota structure and serum metabolic profiles of children with human metapneumovirus (hMPV) infection using 16S rRNA high-throughput sequencing and liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS)-based untargeted metabolomics. Through integrated multi-omics analysis, we aim to explore the correlation between gut microbiota dysbiosis and host metabolic disorder, provide preliminary evidence for potential intervention targets, and offer primary clues for the development of preventive and therapeutic strategies including probiotic supplementation and metaboli
papers.summary: This study used 16S rRNA sequencing and LC-MS-based metabolomics to characterize gut microbiota and serum metabolite changes in children with human metapneumovirus (hMPV) infection. Integrated multi-omics analysis revealed correlations between gut dysbiosis and host metabolic disturbances, suggesting potential targets for probiotic or metabolic interventions.

papers.title: Euonymus alatus in diabetes: a review of phytochemistry, pharmacokinetics, and anti-diabetic mechanisms.
papers.abstract: Euonymus alatus: (EA), a traditional Chinese botanical drug documented in the Shennong Ben Cao Jing, has been investigated for its potential anti-diabetic effects. This review systematically examines the phytochemistry, pharmacokinetics, and anti-diabetic mechanisms of this botanical drug. Over 230 metabolites, including flavonoids, triterpenoids, and lignans, have been identified from EA. Pharmacokinetic studies remain limited; computational predictions suggest that some metabolites may exhibit oral bioavailability, but classical pharmacokinetic parameters have not been experimentally determi
papers.summary: This review consolidates current knowledge on Euonymus alatus, a traditional Chinese medicine, for diabetes treatment, covering its phytochemistry (over 230 metabolites), limited pharmacokinetic data, and proposed anti-diabetic mechanisms. It highlights the need for experimental pharmacokinetic studies to validate computational predictions of oral bioavailability.

papers.title: Effects of Urolithin A supplementation on muscle health outcomes in humans from randomized controlled trials.
papers.abstract: Urolithin A (UA), a gut microbiota-derived metabolite, has been proposed to improve skeletal muscle function, but evidence from randomized controlled trials has not been systematically summarized. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the effects of UA supplementation on muscle performance as well as biochemical and mitochondrial biomarkers in humans.
papers.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluates the effects of Urolithin A (UA), a gut-microbiota-derived metabolite, on muscle health in humans from randomized controlled trials. The findings summarize evidence on muscle performance and biochemical/mitochondrial biomarkers, providing a comprehensive assessment of UA's potential benefits for muscle function.

papers.title: Bacteria-related signals in brain metastases: evidence boundaries, tumor-microenvironment remodeling, and translational prospects.
papers.abstract: Brain metastases (BrM) develop within a highly specialized central nervous system niche shaped by the blood-brain barrier/blood-tumor barrier, brain-resident stromal cells, myeloid populations, and distinct metabolic constraints. Emerging studies suggest that bacteria-related signals can be detected in primary and metastatic brain tumors; however, their biological meaning remains incompletely defined. In particular, low-biomass brain tissues are highly vulnerable to reagent contamination, environmental carry-over, batch effects, and bioinformatic misclassification, making it essential to disti
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: This review examines the emerging but uncertain role of bacteria-related signals in brain metastases, highlighting the technical challenges of studying low-biomass tissues where contamination and misclassification are major concerns. It discusses how these signals may influence the tumor microenvironment and explores their potential as therapeutic targets, while emphasizing the need for rigorous methods to distinguish true biological signals from artifacts.

papers.title: Recombinant Bacillus subtilis spores expressing cholera toxin B and ovalbumin prevent ovalbumin-specific food allergy in mice by upregulating regulatory T cells and modulating gut microbiome flora.
papers.abstract: Although oral immunotherapy has shown clinical efficacy in treating food allergies, its broader implementation is constrained by the occurrence of adverse effects. Consequently, inducing allergen-specific immune tolerance during early life can be a preventive strategy to reduce the development of food allergy.
papers.summary: This study demonstrates that recombinant Bacillus subtilis spores expressing cholera toxin B and ovalbumin can prevent ovalbumin-specific food allergy in mice by upregulating regulatory T cells and modulating the gut microbiome. The findings suggest a potential preventive strategy for food allergies using probiotic-based oral tolerance induction.

papers.title: Dietary index for gut microbiota score is inversely associated with carotid calcified plaque score in ischemic stroke patients.
papers.abstract: Diet influences gut microbiota-derived metabolites, which may affect vascular inflammation and calcification. The Dietary Index for Gut Microbiota (DI-GM) captures dietary patterns hypothesized to support favorable microbial metabolite profiles. In this study, we examined whether higher DI-GM scores are associated with lower carotid calcification burden in ischemic stroke patients and whether trimethylamine N-oxide (TMAO) is statistically associated with this relationship, without implying causality.
papers.summary: This study found that a higher Dietary Index for Gut Microbiota (DI-GM) score, reflecting a diet that supports beneficial gut microbes, is associated with lower carotid artery calcification in ischemic stroke patients. The relationship may involve the gut-derived metabolite TMAO, though the study does not establish causality.

papers.title: Bifidobacterium- and Escherichia-dominant ecological guilds shape altered microbial metabolic capacity of the gut microbiome in tuberculosis patients.
papers.abstract: The gut microbial community plays a key role in maintaining the host immune homeostasis. However, current analytical approaches analyze individual taxa rather than gut communities, thereby missing community-level functions performed by units, such as ecological guilds. Delineating ecological units is a promising approach for summarizing the functional output of microbes and their impact on the host.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This study identifies distinct ecological guilds dominated by Bifidobacterium and Escherichia in the gut microbiomes of tuberculosis patients, showing that these community-level units have altered metabolic capacities compared to healthy controls. The findings suggest that analyzing microbial communities as ecological guilds, rather than individual taxa, can reveal functional changes relevant to tuberculosis pathogenesis.
